method: Each of the eight final PNG files was individually displayed with the local image viewer and visually inspected at 1280 by 800 pixels.
scope: Production OffroadScene and BikeShells; actual seeded eight-rider AI simulation at 10 seconds; prepared procedural materials plus resident photographed scans through the actual ScanStore/PBR loader; neutral component lighting and synthetic backing plane; not the full application scene or hardware FPS acceptance

observations: Photographed fibrous and aggregate grain is visible across the warm beige/tan soil. The broad pink/lavender dirt islands seen in the earlier full-application capture are absent.
Directional travel marks remain visible within the scan detail. Loaded tyre shadows, rider poses, flexible yellow stakes, boulders, canopies and the original event structure are readable.
The plain background and synthetic backing plane identify this as an isolated component scene.
The same fixed rider poses and camera show darker brown soil with cooler, grey-brown wet travel channels; the photographed grain remains readable.
No broad pink/lavender tint or uniform mirror-like sheen is visible. The wet change is restrained and consistent across the exposed riding surface.
The full course route and jump sequence are readable. Most of the surface is brown loam with a greener scanned verge.
Light sand and dark mud regions retain the distinct, partly rectangular boundaries of the existing authored physics zones. The fix did not change course geometry or surface classifications.
Canopies and boulders remain outside the riding band; this overview omits the full application's distant landscape and venue-kit forests.
The broad course surface darkens while the authored sand and mud zones remain distinct. Course shape, dressing and rider poses match the prepared-soil view.
The macro variation remains brown and neutral without the earlier pink soil islands; jump silhouettes stay legible.
The resident dry-earth macro produces a warm tan stadium floor with fine pale and brown aggregate grain, without broad pink/lavender patches.
Jump faces and backsides are visible beyond the riders. Low padded blocks and flexible stakes mark the tight lanes without tall road furniture crossing the riding area.
Repeated spectators, tier aisles and event ribbons frame the bowl. The neutral component lighting does not reproduce the complete main renderer's night presentation.
The same fixed riders and floor geometry are retained while the tan surface becomes darker brown. Photographed grain remains visible through the moisture response.
The berm and jump forms remain readable; no new hue islands or glaring specular patches are visible.
The camera sits inside the bowl below the roof and exposes the floor, trusses, repeated spectator tiers and event ribbons.
The complete jump rhythm and low course markers are legible at overview scale. Fine pale scan grain remains visible without meadow-derived lavender macro islands.
The synthetic backing plane is visible at course cutouts and around the finite terrain ribbon; this image is not the full application floor/venue composition.
The exposed arena floor darkens across the same interior composition; all jumps, course markers, rider positions and roof structure stay fixed.
Moisture produces a brown response while preserving scanned aggregate detail. The surface does not acquire the pink/lavender macro patches previously observed in the full application.
